metaTitle: Portal — Telegram and Delta Chat media bridge
metaDescription: Pair once, then stickers, GIFs, Lottie, and short video move both ways. Prefer self-hosting: you trust whoever runs the bot.
warnBody: A public bot means you trust whoever runs the box. They can see pairing data and whatever you bridge. Delta Chat encryption does not hide that from Portal. Better to run your own.
heroTitle: Stickers and GIFs that survive the jump to Delta Chat.
heroLead: Pair once with a short code. Then send a sticker on Telegram — it shows up in Delta Chat. Send it back the other way. No ugly filenames. No “from Telegram” caption.
ctaPublic: Public bot — you trust the host
posterAlt: Portal branding poster: dark void with the product mark
bridgeLead: After you pair, this goes both ways. We keep filenames boring on purpose — no “from Telegram.”

media.title: Stickers
media.note: The still ones. They land as a sticker or a picture.

media.title: Moving stickers
media.note: Telegram’s animated ones. You get a file, or a GIF if the converter is installed.

media.title: Video stickers
media.note: The short WEBM loops. They show up as video.

media.title: GIFs
media.note: GIFs and Telegram animations (often MP4). They play as GIF or video.

media.title: Custom emoji
media.note: Those premium stickers-in-text. They come through as stickers.

media.title: Text, photos, short clips
media.note: Normal chat stuff, same both ways. Long videos stay on their side — we cap duration.

howTitle: A tunnel: you and the portal, one chat
howLead: Everything you send the portal bot lands in one Delta Chat. Don’t use a public host unless you’re fine with that person seeing what you send. You can also start from Delta Chat with t.me/…?start=CODE.

steps.title: Open the Telegram bot
steps.body: Message @tgdeltabridgebot and send /start in a private chat.

steps.title: Open the Delta Chat invite
steps.body: The bot replies with an invite QR/link and a short pairing code (about 30 minutes).

steps.title: Send the code on Delta Chat
steps.body: Accept the chat, send only the code. The pair becomes active: your Telegram user and that Delta Chat.

steps.title: Send media either way
steps.body: Stickers, GIFs, text, images, short video. Filenames stay neutral; source captions are stripped.

personaNewHint: Mode 1 is the tunnel. Mode 2 is Persona: your bot, their faces.
personaTitle: They write your Telegram bot. You see them as people in Delta Chat.
personaLead: Pairing dumps everything into one chat with the portal. Persona is the other product: you connect a bot you made with BotFather. Friends stay out of a shared pile. Each Telegram person becomes a ghost — a real Delta Chat account with their name and photo — and opens a normal 1:1 with you. What you type there goes out as your bot.
personalCardBody: You talk to the portal bot. Everything lands in one Delta Chat. Good for “my stickers, my chat.”
personaCardBody: They talk to your bot. On Delta Chat Alice looks like Alice, Bob like Bob. Same person later? Same ghost, same chat.
flowLead: Top to bottom. Four hops. That’s the whole trick.

flow.title: Alice DMs your bot
flow.body: She never opens Delta Chat. She only knows the Telegram bot you published.

flow.title: The program is listening on your bot
flow.body: You registered the BotFather token with /pair-bot on the portal (after you /paired yourself).

flow.title: One DC account per Telegram id
flow.body: Missing? Create with PERSONA_ACCOUNT_QR, copy name and photo. Exists? Reuse. Not the same table as personal pairs.

flow.title: Normal 1:1 on Delta Chat
flow.body: No “via Telegram” label. Your reply goes back out through the bot. Telegram cannot puppet Alice as Alice.

setupTitle: You only set this up once
setupBody: mode: persona or both. Pair the portal first so it has your Delta Chat identity. Then in a private chat: /pair-bot <TOKEN>. That token lives in the database on that computer.
groupsBody: Turn on persona.allow_groups, add the bot, turn Group Privacy off in BotFather. The group shows up as TG: … with each speaker as their ghost. Your replies still leave as the bot.
hostTitle: Whoever runs the box is the bot
hostBody: That machine holds the token and the ghost keys. Don’t /pair-bot on a public instance you don’t run.
selfTitle: Best: run it on your machine
selfLead: That’s the version we mean when we say “use this.” One Go binary, deltachat-rpc-server on PATH. You keep the token, the database, the keys.
selfNeeds: The portal binary (build it, or download a GitHub release)
deltachat-rpc-server on PATH and a Telegram BotFather token
Chatmail / Delta Chat provider (e.g. nine.testrun.org for tests)
